what_it_does: Running a large language model (LLM) as a service typically splits the work into two distinct phases: a compute-heavy phase that processes the user's input prompt all at once (called prefill), and a slower, memory-limited phase that generates the output one word at a time (called decoding). WindServe addresses a scheduling problem in systems that run these two phases on separate groups of machines: the prefill machines can get overloaded while decoding machines sit idle, causing users to wait longer than necessary. The system uses a global scheduler that watches resource usage across both pools in real time and dynamically shifts work between them — including the intermediate 'notes' the model keeps during decoding (called KV cache, i.e., the running record of past context) — to keep all machines busy. A stream-based design keeps the two kinds of work from interfering with each other even when they briefly share the same hardware.
